items.body:

items.claim: Public writeup evidence for xss: Blob-URL sandbox escape to XSS.
items.body:

Reason it matters: Blob-URL sandbox escape to XSS.

One obvious solution is getting a separate domain to generate the blobs for you, that has nothing shared with Shazzer, so an XSS on that domain doesn't grant access to Shazzer's cookies.

CORROBORATING PUBLISHER (owasp.org) on the same weakness class:
For JSON, verify that the Content-Type header is application/json and not text/html to prevent XSS.

items.claim: Public writeup evidence for smuggling: HTTP/2 framing WAF bypass.
items.body:
HARVESTED FROM bugbountydaily RSS -> https://lab.ctbb.show/research/h2-WAF-Bypasses
Reason it matters: HTTP/2 framing WAF bypass.

The proxy sends a sub-request to an auth service containing only the request headers - because that is where authentication data lives (Authorization headers, cookies, session tokens).

CORROBORATING PUBLISHER (mitre.org) on the same weakness class:
The interpretation of HTTP responses can be manipulated if response headers include a space between the header name and colon, or if HTTP 1.1 headers are sent through a proxy configured for HTTP 1.0, allowing for HTTP response smuggling.

items.claim: Public writeup evidence for supply_chain: CI workflow -> supply chain.
items.body:
HARVESTED FROM bugbountydaily RSS -> https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/
Reason it matters: CI workflow -> supply chain.

The gh CLI accepts URLs as positional arguments, so a prompt injection payload can instruct Claude to embed secret values in the URL path or query parameters (e.g., gh issue view https://example.com/ ), sending the secrets to an attacker-controlled server.

CORROBORATING PUBLISHER (owasp.org) on the same weakness class:
Attacks against deserializers have been found to allow denial-of-service, access control, or remote code execution (RCE) attacks.
